lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: kitchen tool, heat, and appliance safety

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic kitchen tool, heat, and appliance safety task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With a trusted adult present the entire time, the learner chooses one real kitchen tool, heat source, or appliance from the guidance sheet's list, explains the specific safety risk it poses, and demonstrates the correct safe-handling technique for it once while the adult watches and confirms it was done correctly.
safetyNotes: The learner only demonstrates the chosen technique with the trusted adult present and watching the entire time.
The learner does not use a knife, stove, or oven unsupervised at any point during or after this lesson.
Completing this task sheet never certifies the demonstration by itself; a guardian confirmation is required before the task counts as complete.

simulationAlternative.description: If real handling is not possible, the learner instead reviews the provided set of six short tool-handling scenario descriptions (such as a hand position on a knife, a pot handle position on a stove, or a way of removing a hot pan) and sorts each as safe or unsafe, explaining the specific reason for each call using the same safety criteria as the real demonstration.

materials: adult-or-local: access to the real kitchen with a trusted adult present
adult-or-local: the provided kitchen tool and appliance safety guidance sheet
adult-or-local: one real kitchen tool, heat source, or appliance from the guidance sheet's list
learner-local: an oven mitt if the chosen demonstration involves a hot item

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one specific situation in the future where forgetting this safety habit could lead to an injury, and name the exact step you will remember to prevent it.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u03-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Risk identification: The named risk correctly and specifically describes how the chosen item could cause injury if mishandled. | Safe technique demonstration: The adult confirms the demonstrated technique correctly matched the guidance sheet, with or without one correction. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner choose a second tool, heat source, or appliance from the guidance sheet's list and repeat the full demonstration and explanation process for it, comparing what risk it shares with the first item and what risk is different.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: kitchen tool, heat, and appliance safety worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a trusted adult present the entire time, the learner chooses one real kitchen tool, heat source, or appliance from the guidance sheet's list, explains the specific safety risk it poses, and demonstrates the correct safe-handling technique for it once while the adult watches and confirms it was done correctly.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact kitchen tool, heat, and appliance safety decision or action.
Model move 2: Before demonstrating, choose one tool, heat source, or appliance from the guidance sheet and name the specific risk it poses if handled incorrectly.
Model move 3: With your adult, review the guidance sheet's correct technique for your chosen item before demonstrating it.

Model check: Risk identification: The named risk correctly and specifically describes how the chosen item could cause injury if mishandled. | Safe technique demonstration: The adult confirms the demonstrated technique correctly matched the guidance sheet, with or without one correction.

resources.title: kitchen tool, heat, and appliance safety action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for kitchen tool, heat, and appliance safety.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: kitchen tool, heat, and appliance safety coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a trusted adult present the entire time, the learner chooses one real kitchen tool, heat source, or appliance from the guidance sheet's list, explains the specific safety risk it poses, and demonstrates the correct safe-handling technique for it once while the adult watches and confirms it was done correctly.
Coach direction: Before demonstrating, choose one tool, heat source, or appliance from the guidance sheet and name the specific risk it poses if handled incorrectly.
Learner prompt: Name the tool, heat source, or appliance you chose and describe the specific injury or hazard that incorrect handling could cause.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: kitchen tool, heat, and appliance safety complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult, review the guidance sheet's correct technique for your chosen item before demonstrating it.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I read the guidance sheet's correct technique for my chosen item before attempting it.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Describe the correct technique in your own words, naming the specific hand or body position involved.

Equal-access rule: If real handling is not possible, the learner instead reviews the provided set of six short tool-handling scenario descriptions (such as a hand position on a knife, a pot handle position on a stove, or a way of removing a hot pan) and sorts each as safe or unsafe, explaining the specific reason for each call using the same safety criteria as the real demonstration.

resources.title: kitchen tool, heat, and appliance safety minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one specific situation in the future where forgetting this safety habit could lead to an injury, and name the exact step you will remember to prevent it.

Success checks: Risk identification: The named risk correctly and specifically describes how the chosen item could cause injury if mishandled. | Safe technique demonstration: The adult confirms the demonstrated technique correctly matched the guidance sheet, with or without one correction.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: kitchen tool, heat, and appliance safety supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u03-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional kitchen tool, heat, and appliance safety condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Risk identification: The named risk correctly and specifically describes how the chosen item could cause injury if mishandled. | Safe technique demonstration: The adult confirms the demonstrated technique correctly matched the guidance sheet, with or without one correction..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u03-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.

retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
